title: Store spec: table-aware fetch fake + tests for dataset statuses, reset, and stale-search guard
description:
src/property-history/__tests__/propertyHistoryStore.spec.ts was written when the store only looked up the address. The store now also loads permits and investigations (loadAllDatasets with Promise.all), and the spec has not caught up.

Known problem in the existing spec: the "holds the address after a successful search" test uses stubAisFound(), which answers EVERY fetch with the AIS body. The two gateway calls get that body too, fetchAllRows throws on the missing `data`, and the store silently sets permitsStatus and investigationsStatus to 'error'. The test passes because it never reads them. Adding `expect(store.permitsStatus).toBe('loaded')` makes it fail.

Step 1 (Claude drafts, new pattern): a test fake in src/__tests__/fakeServices.ts that routes by the `table` query parameter, e.g. stubServices({ permits: samplePermitRows, case_investigations: sampleInvestigationRows }), and can be told to fail one table. Replaces stubAisFoundAndPermits (used by PropertyHistoryView.spec.ts). The view tests and every later dataset need the same thing.

Step 2 (Andy writes, same shape as the existing tests): store tests for
- after a found address, permitsStatus and investigationsStatus reach 'loaded' with the fixture rows
- one dataset failing (gateway 500 for one table) leaves the other 'loaded' and its own status 'error'
- a new search resets the previous property's permits and investigations to [] / 'idle' before the lookup answers
- the stale-search guard: start search A, start search B before A's fetch resolves, A's results never land (needs a fetch stub whose promise is resolved by hand, e.g. a deferred promise per call)

Fixtures stay on 1234 MARKET ST.

title: Ask CityGeo to document that databridge timestamps are Philadelphia clock readings (no zone)
description:
databridge-api returns timestamps as the table's LOCAL clock reading instead of UTC, and `src/shared/databridge.ts` works around it in `normalizeTimestamps()` (every timestamp-looking string in every row is read as local time and relabeled as real UTC). vue3-atlas and L-I-Consolidation carry the same workaround.

Verified 2026-10-07 on `permits` / `permitnumber = 'RP-2022-005991'` / `permitissuedate`:
- databridge: `2022-06-15T00:00:00` (bare local reading)
- Carto, same row: `2022-06-15T04:00:00Z` (correct UTC)
- normalizeTimestamps(databridge value) == Carto value

Some queries (seen with ORDER BY, per atlas) return the local reading with a false `.000Z` suffix instead; the regex handles both forms.

TODO:
1. Report to CityGeo (gateway owners) — Andy has the paste-able report from the 2026-10-07 chat. Ask for a heads-up before any fix ships.
2. When the gateway starts returning real UTC, `normalizeTimestamps` would shift correct values AGAIN. Remove it (and its tests in `src/shared/__tests__/databridge.spec.ts`) in the same release the gateway fix lands. The spec's live test can be extended to assert the raw gateway string ends in `Z` with a non-midnight hour for RP-2022-005991 to detect the change.
notes: REFRAMED 2026-10-08 after a morning of probing (Andy cancelled the Alex/Roland meeting): this is NOT a bug. The gateway consistently returns timestamptz columns as the Philadelphia wall-clock reading with no zone, from both its PostgREST and Carto backends (service=carto gives the same string; Carto called directly gives the same instant as UTC). Verified on permits.permitissuedate (summer) and splits.election_date (winter). The .000Z form noted in atlas (Sept 2026) could not be reproduced today on any query form. Our code treats readings as America/New_York explicitly at the door (date-fns-tz fromZonedTime in src/shared/databridge.ts) and displays in America/New_York (formatInTimeZone in src/shared/formatDate.ts); the live permits test would go red if the format changed. ASK: CityGeo documents the convention (or, optionally, adds an offset like -04:00, which keeps the human-readable value and removes ambiguity). Nothing to remove on our side either way. Side note for vue3-atlas / L-I-Consolidation: their normalizeTimestamps uses the viewer's local zone and their display formats in local, so non-Eastern viewers see dates shifted by a day; port the explicit-zone approach back when convenient.
close_reason: Gateway now sends real UTC (2026-10-23); normalizeTimestamps respells labeled forms as Z and keeps the bare fallback

comments.author: rothwell.andy@gmail.com
comments.text:
UPDATE 2026-10-21: the .000Z form IS reproducible, and the 10/08 "could not be reproduced" was a probing gap. The trigger is the `sql=` code path on the Carto V3 backend, which the 10/08 probes never hit (table= with service=carto returns bare; a simple sql= gets served by PostgREST and returns bare).

Minimal pair, same row, both pinned service=carto:
- table=appeals&fields=appealnumber,scheduleddate,createddate&where=appealnumber = 'HA-2025-004128'  ->  scheduleddate "2026-09-02T09:30:00" (bare)
- sql=SELECT appealnumber, scheduleddate, createddate FROM appeals WHERE appealnumber = 'HA-2025-004128'  ->  scheduleddate "2026-09-02T09:30:00.000Z" (false UTC label; Carto called directly says 13:30:00Z)

Any SQL function in a sql= statement (DATE() in the WHERE, st_astext() in the SELECT) routes it off PostgREST to Carto V3, so L-I-Consolidation's appeals calendar query gets the Z form on every load. The atlas "ORDER BY" theory was wrong. table= on PostgREST, Carto and AGO all return the bare form, so the backend fallback is transparent for table= queries.

Reported to CityGeo by Andy on 2026-10-21 with the minimal pair above.

Risk for THIS repo: src/shared/databridge.ts BARE_TIMESTAMP matches only the bare form. Safe while the app is table=-only, but a future sql= query served by Carto V3 would pass the Z form through un-normalized (4-5 h wrong). atlas and L-I-Consolidation regexes accept both forms. When CityGeo fixes the Z (or starts sending real UTC), re-check all three normalizers before celebrating.

title: AIS opa_owners arrives as a list; the results page prints it raw with brackets
description:
Seen 2026-10-14 on 1234 MARKET ST: the Owner line on PropertyHistoryResults.vue shows `[ "SEPTA" ]`, brackets and quotes included.

The MuleSoft AIS endpoint (api-prod.phila.gov/ais/v1) returns `opa_owners` as an ARRAY. The old api.phila.gov/ais/li endpoint returned a plain string, which is what the first probe (2026-10-02) saw, so `AddressRecord.owners` was typed as `string` and the page prints it raw.

Fix:
- `src/shared/ais.ts`: type `AisProperties.opa_owners` as `string[] | string | null`; make `AddressRecord.owners` a `string[]` (wrap a plain string in a list; null → []).
- `PropertyHistoryResults.vue`: join for display (`owners.join(', ')`).
- Update `src/__tests__/fakeAis.ts` `sampleProperties.opa_owners` to an array and `ais.spec.ts` expectations.
- Check a multi-owner address so the joined display is seen once for real.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-10-14: AisProperties.opa_owners typed string[] | null, AddressRecord.owners joined with ', ', null guarded; fixture typed as AisProperties; tests for two owners and null.

title: Contractor lookup: aggregate violations server-side, never fetch the citywide set
description:
Design the contractor lookup so it never fetches the citywide contractor_violations set.

CONTEXT (from L-I-Consolidation, branch wip/databridge-api-migration, 2026-10-21):
The old app's Find a Licensed Contractor page (src/layouts/ContractorLookup.vue, getContractorViolations) pulls EVERY contractor violation to the browser on every page load:
  table=contractor_violations
  where=NOT (licensetype IN ('Electrical Inspection Agency','Electrical Inspector')) AND violationnumber IS NOT NULL
That is ~19,459 rows (count_only, 2026-10-21), fetched as a keyset walk of 20 sequential 999-row requests, ~28 MB transferred, ~6 s. The gateway caps table= replies at 1,000 rows, so any "fetch everything" dataset becomes a walk like this. Andy saw the 20 requests in the Network tab and called it "a little crazy"; it is being left as-is in the old app because that app is being abandoned.

The rows are used for (a) a per-contractor violation count and (b) violationdate2year (violations within the last 2 years), joined client-side to the contractor list.

WHY THE OLD APP DIDN'T NEED THIS:
The contractor LIST query on the same page already aggregates on the server:
  WITH cv AS (SELECT licensenumber, count(*) ... FROM contractor_violations GROUP BY licensenumber), rpb AS (...)
  SELECT ... FROM trade_licenses LEFT JOIN cv ... LEFT JOIN rpb ... ORDER BY ... LIMIT/OFFSET
(ContractorLookup.vue ~L452-507, sql= on databridge). So the per-contractor count is already computed server-side; the citywide client-side fetch duplicates it.

DIRECTION FOR li.phila.gov:
- List view: get violation counts (total, and within-2-years if needed) from a server-side aggregate - either a date-filtered count inside the same sql= CTE, or a CityGeo-provided summary table/view (e.g. contractor_violations_summary keyed by licensenumber) that table= can hit with no walk.
- Detail view: fetch one contractor's violations on demand with table=contractor_violations&where=licensenumber = 'X' - small result, PostgREST, single request, no walk.
- Never load a citywide table into the browser to join client-side.

GOTCHAS:
- PostgREST rejects `x NOT IN (...)`; write `NOT (x IN (...))` or the gateway silently falls through to Carto V3 (verified 2026-10-21: meta.service flips between "Databridge-Public PostgREST API" and "Carto V3 SQL API").
- The gateway's response envelope has meta.service (which backend answered) and links.next (the gateway builds the objectid keyset cursor itself, order=objectid) - useful for checking in the Network tab.
- contractor_violations and trade_licenses are not queried by vue3-atlas; there is no reference implementation to port. The old app's CTE query is the closest thing.
- If a summary table is the answer, that is a CityGeo ask (see the atlas handoff's ask list for the format).

comments.author: rothwell.andy@gmail.com
comments.text:
2026-10-21 addendum: the contractor lookup page has FOUR other sql= queries besides the violations walk, and all four are served by Carto V3 today (verified via meta.service). What each would take to move off sql= in li.phila.gov:

1. `SELECT DISTINCT licensetype FROM trade_licenses WHERE licensetype NOT IN (...) ORDER BY licensetype` (26 values, Contractor type dropdown). table= has no DISTINCT. Options: hardcode (types change occasionally), ask CityGeo for a lookup view, or accept one small sql=. Do NOT walk 48,733 licenses to dedupe.

2. `SELECT DISTINCT licensestatus ...` (6 values, Contractor status dropdown). Same; hardcoding 6 statuses is reasonable.

3. `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trade_licenses WHERE <filters>` (result count). CAN move: `table=trade_licenses&count_only=true&where=<same filters>` returns meta.records_total on PostgREST (verified: 48,733 with the type exclusion). Two requirements: the transport needs count_only support, and the keyword filter `lower(contactname) LIKE '%x%'` must become `contactname ILIKE '%x%'` (PostgREST rejects a function on the left of a comparison; ILIKE is supported). Also `x NOT IN (...)` must be written `NOT (x IN (...))`.

4. `WITH cv AS (SELECT licensenumber, count(*) FROM contractor_violations ... GROUP BY licensenumber), rpb AS (SELECT * FROM resp_party_balance) SELECT ... FROM trade_licenses tl LEFT JOIN cv ... LEFT JOIN rpb ... WHERE <filters> ORDER BY <user-chosen column> LIMIT 25 OFFSET n` (the contractor list, server-side paged and sorted). CANNOT move with today's gateway: table= can't join, can't sort server-side, has no OFFSET (its params are table, fields, where, limit, count_only, out_sr, sql, timeout, max_age). The only non-sql path is walking all 48,733 licenses into the browser and joining/sorting/paging client-side, which is worse than the violations walk this bead is about. Either accept the contractor list as a legitimate sql= use, or ask CityGeo for (a) a view that precomputes violation count + balance per license AND (b) server-side order/offset on table= - both are needed, (a) alone doesn't help.

Decision for L-I-Consolidation (old app): all four left as-is on 2026-10-21; #4 can't move and #1-3 are sub-100 ms requests.

title: Agree missing-status display text; fix old app and rewrite together
description:
Decide the display text for a missing/null record status and apply it to BOTH apps at once: the old L-I-Consolidation app (small fix, Andy says the current "Not Available" may be wrong) and this rewrite.

Context:
- Old app, store/index.js investigationsResults(): replaces a null investigationstatus with "Not Available". Violations use "Not Available" for a null caseprioritydesc too. The old-app fix is planned for the same working session as this rewrite step so the wording matches.
- Rewrite: toInvestigation() and toPermit() deliberately do NOT substitute anything; a missing status is "" in the record. The fallback text belongs in the view when the results tables are built (decided 2026-10-14).
- Real data: 1234 Market St case_investigations rows have investigationstatus PASSED/FAILED; investigationtype is null on every row seen, so "type" will often be "".

Done when: old app shows the agreed text, and the rewrite's investigations (and permits) table shows the same text for a missing status, with a test.

title: Property History search box doesn't follow Back/Forward: URL address changes but the box keeps the old text
description: In src/property-history/PropertyHistoryView.vue the search box ref 'address' is seeded ONCE from route.query.address. Search A, then B, then press Back: the URL and results return to A (PropertyHistoryResults.vue watches the route) but the box still shows B. Fix: a one-way watch on route.query.address that writes into address.value when it changes (NOT a computed — the box must stay the user's to type in). Four lines. Found 2026-10-13 while reviewing.
close_reason: Decided 2026-10-14: the search box keeps the user's text on Back/Forward. The breadcrumb and the Address line both show the current property, so there is no mismatch to fix. Not a bug.

title: Case detail page must handle investigations whose case has no violation rows (old app breaks)
description:
The old app's violation detail page is really a CASE page: it shows the case fields, the case's violations, and (at the bottom) the case's investigations. Clicking an investigation row on the results page opens that same page by looking up the VIOLATION case with the same casenumber (SearchResults.vue openDetail: `value = this.$store.state.violationResults.msg[value.casenumber]`). There is no investigation detail page.

Flaw in the old app: an investigation whose case has no violation rows has nothing to open. Real numbers for 1234 MARKET ST (2026-10-20): 99 investigations across 42 cases; 33 violation cases; 13 investigation cases have NO violation rows (e.g. 322900, 40344, 48457); 4 violation cases have no investigations. The old code has no guard, so ~1/3 of investigation clicks at this property hit a missing case. Verify by clicking case 322900 in the old app.

Decision needed when the detail page is built: a case page that composes whatever exists for a casenumber: case fields (from the ViolationCase if there is one, else from the Investigation row, which also carries casetype/priority/responsibility/address), the violations list (may be empty), the investigations list (may be empty). Our data layer already supports this: Investigation.caseNumber and ViolationCase.caseNumber, nothing pre-joined; the join is a find by case number at page level.

Also for that page: the old app's violation detail rows (Case number, Priority, Date added, Date updated = mostrecentinvestigation, Resolution date = casecompleteddate, Documents = publicnov link) and per-violation rows (code, type = violationcodetitle, date, status, plus a code explanation looked up from a violationShortDesc list).
